13. Visit dates, one idea at a time

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-06-visits.Rmd
book-06-visits.Rmd

What you will learn

Separate day offsets from calendar dates, select visit settings and build one row per visit.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

Choose an anchor

An anchor is the date from which you measure time. Here it is the public fixed date 2020-01-01. A day offset of zero means that date; negative values mean earlier.

visit <- omop_event("visit_occurrence")
all_visits <- omop_window(NULL, NULL, anchor = "2020-01-01")
class(all_visits)
#> [1] "omop_window" "list"

Both window ends are unbounded. The anchor defines the scale, not a restriction to visits after January 1.

First and last visit as day offsets 

first <- omop_variable(event = visit,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_date", window = all_visits))
last <- omop_variable(event = visit,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_date", window = all_visits))
class(first)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

These reducers return integer days relative to the window anchor, not R Date objects. People without visits retain missing values.

offsets <- omop_recipe(variables = list(first_days = first, last_days = last),
  outputs = omop_output("visits", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(offsets, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(offsets, out = c(visits = "D_offsets"), conns = conns))
#>      visits 
#> "D_offsets"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_offsets$first_days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean 
#>  73.0000  73.0000  73.0000 166.0000 201.0000 201.0000 201.0000 146.6667

The summary is an aggregate of private offsets. It is not a list of visit dates.

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_offsets$last_days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>        5%       10%       25%       50%       75%       90%       95%      Mean 
#>  201.0000  201.0000  201.0000  439.0000 1369.0000 1369.0000 1369.0000  669.6667

Some people have later visits. Taking a last date answers a different question from taking the first; it does not describe duration of observation.

Use a shortcut with an indexed study

The shortcuts omop_first_date() and omop_last_date() use the study index as their reference. An index selects the event that begins a person’s study episode. Here each first visit is the index, so its first-visit offset is zero.

visit_study <- omop_study(visit, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(first_days = omop_first_date("visit_occurrence"),
                  last_days = omop_last_date("visit_occurrence")))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(visit_study, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(visit_study, out = c(baseline = "D_visit_study"), conns = conns))
#>        baseline 
#> "D_visit_study"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_visit_study$first_days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 18
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>    0    0    0    0    0    0    0    0

This is the simple layer of the same language-2 API. It expands into an ordinary recipe. It includes people with an eligible index visit, so unlike our all-person wide table it excludes the people who never visited.

Assign an actual calendar date 

calendar <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visit_date = omop_date("first_visit")),
  outputs = omop_output("visits", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(calendar, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(calendar, out = c(visits = "D_calendar"), conns = conns))
#>       visits 
#> "D_calendar"

omop_date() defaults to day precision and assigns a Date on the server. An exact date is a class-2 quasi-identifier: a value that can help identify someone when combined with other information. The released assign path permits it without an owner-side absolute-date switch. The analyst still cannot fetch its rows.

For a useful categorical aggregate, explicitly choose month precision:

months <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visit_month = omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "month", level_range = c("2020-03-01", "2020-07-31")))),
  outputs = omop_output("visits", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(months, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(months, out = c(visits = "D_months"), conns = conns))
#>     visits 
#> "D_months"
ds.omop.table("D_months", "visit_month", conns = conns)
#> D_months$visit_month
#> 2020-03 2020-04 2020-05 2020-06 2020-07 
#>       6       0       0       6       6

The public range declares month categories, including empty months. It is a study definition, not a range discovered by requesting minimum and maximum patient dates. The factor labels use year-month order so that they sort chronologically.

Filter inpatient or outpatient visits

In OMOP, these settings are concepts in visit_concept_id. The separate visit_type_concept_id describes provenance. Inspect the settings by name:

settings <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(9201L, 9202L), conns = conns)
settings$pooled["concept_name"]
#>       concept_name
#> 1  Inpatient Visit
#> 2 Outpatient Visit
inpatient <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = 9201L)
setting <- omop_variable(event = inpatient,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "visit_concept_id"))
class(setting)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The event filter keeps inpatient records; the reducer reads the setting of the first such record. People without inpatient records have a missing setting.

inpatient_people <- omop_recipe(variables = list(setting = setting),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(inpatient_people, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(inpatient_people, out = c(people = "D_inpatient"), conns = conns))
#>        people 
#> "D_inpatient"
ds.omop.table("D_inpatient", "setting", conns = conns)
#> D_inpatient$setting
#> Inpatient Visit 
#>              12

This counts people with an inpatient setting, not total inpatient visits.

Keep one row per visit

A long output retains event rows. Register an event named visits and ask for its records. Long outputs normalise the source date to start_date and the setting to concept_id. Day precision keeps actual calendar dates:

long_visits <- omop_recipe(
  events = list(visits = omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")),
  outputs = omop_output("visits", format = "long", sources = "visits"),
  date_spec = omop_date_spec(precision = "day"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(long_visits, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(long_visits, out = c(visits = "D_visits"), conns = conns))
#>     visits 
#> "D_visits"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_visits", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"                "cohort_row_id"         "person_id"            
#> [4] "concept_id"            "start_date"            "end_date"             
#> [7] "visit_type_concept_id"

The column inventory describes a private table. It does not return a visit row. The source’s visit_start_date is now called start_date. If your analysis needs the source spelling, add a value-preserving alias on the server:

print(ds.omop.mutate("D_visits", visit_start_date = start_date,
                     newobj = "D_visit_dates", conns = conns))
#> [1] "D_visit_dates"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_visit_dates", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"                "cohort_row_id"         "person_id"            
#> [4] "concept_id"            "start_date"            "end_date"             
#> [7] "visit_type_concept_id" "visit_start_date"

This copies the date column inside the protected table. It preserves one row per visit and returns only the new symbol name and column names.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_visits$concept_id", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                    study
#> D_visits$concept_id site
#>    Inpatient Visit     1
#>    Outpatient Visit    1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                    study
#> D_visits$concept_id site
#>    Inpatient Visit   0.4
#>    Outpatient Visit  0.6
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                    study
#> D_visits$concept_id site
#>    Inpatient Visit    12
#>    Outpatient Visit   18
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_visits$concept_id
#>  Inpatient Visit Outpatient Visit 
#>              0.4              0.6 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_visits$concept_id
#>  Inpatient Visit Outpatient Visit 
#>               12               18 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

These are counts of visit records by translated setting. A person can contribute several visits, so do not call these counts numbers of distinct people.

Recap

Choose offsets for elapsed time and omop_date for calendar presentation. Wide selects one value per person; long keeps visit rows privately.

Try it

Use a typed parameter to make the setting recipe reusable, bind it to outpatient visits, and count the translated setting.

Solution

setting_id <- omop_param("setting", type = "concept_set")
template <- omop_recipe(variables = list(setting = omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = setting_id),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "visit_concept_id"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
outpatient <- recipe_bind(template, setting = 9202L)
stopifnot(recipe_explain(outpatient, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(outpatient, out = c(people = "D_outpatient"), conns = conns))
#>         people 
#> "D_outpatient"
ds.omop.table("D_outpatient", "setting", conns = conns)
#> D_outpatient$setting
#> Outpatient Visit 
#>               18
